ledger-name.note:
The ADR must make a very clear and usable, actionable proposal that will allow users to properly fulfil the ledger data keeping. Every single transaction row must be associated with references after it has been categorised by spending category and business category and normalised. This is the way we can integrate base rates, VAT rates, and proportionality metadata related to the tax filing amounts.
I hope I'm making myself clear. I want to clarify why invoices and receipts are being conflated when it comes to spending transactions that are to be categorised as aggregate segments of the tax filing data, versus completely different categories of:
- autonomous issued
- business issued and received invoices
These relate to work being rendered or money being owed to the filer. The conflation still remains and is extremely confusing. Why?

Feels like you are misunderstanding what receipts are. Receipts are required column data for transactions and are part of the sanitization process. Metadata must support a transaction to be text calculation eligible. This needs reviewing. Do a much better job

statement-imports.note: Okay so I think yes. Whilst internally we do support import statements, I do wonder whether we should generalise the statement command into simply as a --statement {provider|defaults to auto} structure and use ledger import {flags}

transactions.note:
We have reached the main point of contention. I need this to be conditional on the actual decisions we have to make to decide whether transactions are the only supported elements in the ledger.
Where will we be storing ledgers, statements, invoices, and receipts? Will you confirm that tax invoices that are unrelated to purchases of goods and services are a separate entity and not part of the ledger?
Once the conflation has been resolved, I need us to consider whether the ledger should automatically carry the list function without structuring it under transactions. Alternatively we could create a generalised data subdomain that has lists, search, and a robust database filter (query, range, description, category, and so forth). The database filter should support regex and so forth. This is a new feature that we have not yet implemented, and the eCLI re-implementation must factor it into the scope of the actual refactor.
It is also very clear that the ledger data or transactions subcommand needs to have two operation modes:
1. Read-only
2. Edit mode
The edit mode will be highly conditional on the functionality required but should support all of the operations that the internal Python library supports (I assume it supports:
- Splitting
- Categorising
- Manually tagging
- Enriching
- Method setting
- Editing
- Data tags
- Flags
- Model associations
- and so forth
I am unsure about the full coverage, but the CLI must be cross-referenced against the Python CLI and the Python API

To recap, consider explicitly creating edit and search subdomains either within Ledger or within the transactions subdomain. I prefer to keep the list not overly nested. I think
- `aeat app ledger search | edit` would be a good design

calculation.note:
Yeah okay so I suppose that's good but I think this is just a shallow assumption and the actual design of it is lacking. I do not understand what commands the `calculate` will utilise.

Default text flow for any given declaration requires that all indrawed modello, depending on the time of the year and the filing deadlines and the outstanding status in AE 80 (previously filed, missing, to be revised, etc.), be calculated. Calculations will mandate what actually needs to be calculated. It also depends on the ledger status, whether everything is properly sanitised, categorised, and whether checks and calculations are robustly retained and double-accounted so that shifts, changes, and trends, and edits that might exist in any given current state are actually checked against filed and stable filing conditions.

All of these are considerations that the `calculate` command should and must actually implement and consider. This is a massive multi-wave audit request. The CLI needs to be designed on top of the proper, robust understanding and baseline functionality of the BIFO modules.

I propose that declaration has a command similar to `calculate` but `SH` needs to be changed to `review`. The export format needs to be exposed to all commands that are outputting any meaningful data for human review. The current CLI is completely missing all user review updates where manual calculation edits would need to be factored into any automatic calculation based on ledger data. Remember, whilst yes we are absolutely using ledger data for deriving the base calculations for modellers, every single element must be human editable and review-gated. The CI should not ever allow a modello calculation to be considered approved if it has not been reviewed by a human and explicitly marked as such.

Again, massive request to review the Python backend to ensure these gates exist in the actual codebase and the functionality is in place.
